name: autonovel
tagline: An autonomous pipeline for writing, revising, typesetting, illustrating, and narrating a complete novel — from seed concept to print-ready PDF, ePub, audiobook, and landing page.
core_features: Five-phase novel production pipeline: Foundation → First Draft → Automated Revision → Opus Review Loop → Export
World bible generation from seed concept
Character registry with arcs and relationships
24-chapter outline with beats and foreshadowing ledger
Sequential chapter drafting with anti-pattern rules
Mechanical slop detection (regex-based banned words, clichés, show-don't-tell violations)
Adversarial editing ("cut 500 words" analysis with classified cuts)
Dual-persona review (literary critic + professor of fiction) via Claude Opus
LaTeX typesetting with EB Garamond font (trade paperback format)
Cover art and chapter ornament generation
Multi-voice audiobook generation with speaker-attributed segments
Propagation debt tracking across 5 co-evolving layers
ai_capabilities: Autonomous world bible, character, and outline generation
Sequential chapter drafting with context loading (voice + world + characters + previous chapter)
LLM judge evaluation (prose quality, voice adherence, character distinctiveness, beat coverage)
Self-evaluation with keep/discard loop based on scores
Dual-persona deep review (Claude Opus as literary critic and professor of fiction)

tech_stack.ui: Static HTML/CSS landing page (no framework), LaTeX typesetting

target_users: Writers seeking AI-assisted novel production, developers interested in autonomous creative pipelines, publishers exploring AI-generated content workflows
license: information unavailable (no LICENSE file found in repository)
strengths: Complete end-to-end pipeline from concept to finished products (PDF, ePub, audiobook, landing page)
Two-layer quality control: mechanical regex scanning + LLM judge evaluation
Sophisticated dual-persona review loop with Claude Opus for deep prose analysis
Five co-evolving document layers with propagation debt tracking
Proven production history: first novel "The Second Son of the House of Bells" at 79,456 words
Comprehensive anti-slop and anti-pattern detection systems
Extensive craft education embedded (Save the Cat, Story Circle, Sanderson frameworks)
Branch-based per-novel workflow (framework on master, content on branches)
Git-based version control with keep/discard commits
weaknesses: Requires paid API keys (Anthropic required, fal.ai and ElevenLabs optional) — not self-hostable for core functionality
No explicit open-source license file in repository
Only 2 contributors, indicating limited community contribution
Python-only, no GUI or web interface for non-technical users
Very minimal Python dependencies (only httpx and python-dotenv) — most logic is prompt-driven
Last update was March 2026, may not be actively maintained
No issue tracking or community discussion infrastructure visible
